Voatdev

Last week in /v/voatdev was more active than the week before, but still not thriving with life. It began with a report about issues with making use of what are supposed to be three stickies per subverse. Issues with the auto-toggle stickies have been documented before, but it's possible these issues go beyond just that.

There was also a post where a development-experienced user offered help (responses to such offers have historically involved redirecting users to Voat's GitHub, where they have the opportunity to attempt to resolve any issues that might stand out, although with the public codebase being out of date -- due to general lack of help and the general advantage it gives to malevolent agents -- I am unsure whether such a response would be likely at present). Such a post as this being made after the announcement about Voat finding an Angel (more on that below) is not at all surprising.

Other than these, there were a couple ([1] | [2]) of suggestion / discussion posts.

VoatStatistics

Posts per day for last week: Friday had the most submissions last week at 1,887; the total number of submissions side-wide was 11,459, down from 14,442 the week before, which is an expected decrease considering Christmas fell within last week. Friday also had the most comments last week at 18,310, with 108,500 total site-wide, down from 123,445 the week before for the above-stated reason.

Most commented posts for last week: Excepting the aforementioned announcement, a post where a user expressed concern at his girlfriend's apparent refusal to ever have children was the most commented last week. Considering how seriously the majority of Voat users take family and the proliferation of genes and stakes in the future, a large response to such a concern as this is not surprising. Once again I am pleased to see community topics at the top!

Most controversial posts last week: For what I think is the first time since /v/aww posts started appearing on these lists, all 20 of the top 20 most controversial posts last week were from /v/aww. Putt did state that he intended to address the /v/aww issue in some way, but exactly what aspect of the issue he meant is unclear. He might have been referring to the gore posts that have been made there, and originated this whole controversy, or he might have been referring to what might in fact be vote manipulation of some kind taking place within the subverse. I find it very unlikely that he meant the low quality posts that have been attracting all the downvotes, since these posts fit within the rules of the subverse and do not violate any of Voat's rules (except for the fact that vote manipulation may be being used to get these posts to the front page).

Voat Updates

As far as I observed, nothing notable occurred on Voat this past week. Why should it; it's Christmas season! Go be with your family, goats, and let us hope Putts and Cyn and our shadow lurker Atko have the opportunity to do the same this season.

O how wrong a man can be! Christmas season or not, it is clear that Putt has indeed been working tirelessly to come to an agreement with an Angel, a financier, a sponsor of Voat. He assured us all in the Christmas day announcement on this topic that neither Voat's freedom of speech devotion nor its intention to protect user privacy would be negatively affected by the sponsorship, and in fact Putt implied that Voat would be doing more work than ever to protect user privacy. He also stated that this arrangement would grant him full-time access to Voat, and the development potential of this statement alone is truly incredible.

There are several concerns and perspectives and questions that people have raised, and I have many thoughts of my own on this change, but if I expressed them all here this post would be so long that no one would read it. Perhaps I will make a post here another time to delve deeper into the implications and concerns raised by this truly monumental milestone in Voat's history. We will have to be more vigilant than ever before moving forward, but Putt has a very good record of taking actions and making judgments that are in the best interests of Voat as a freedom platform, and we have no reason to believe that this case will be any different, and every reason to believe that his assurances that the freedom of speech and privacy interests of Voat will remain. Let us move forward as all wise goats should: as optimists -- who bring our raincoats.
